stories.h: Gunman in Krakow Main Square shooting that killed six dies in hospital
stories.p: The 24-year-old suspected gunman in a shooting in Krakow's Main Square that killed six people and injured about 16 has died in hospital, Polish police say. Three of his relatives were also found dead at his home.
body: The suspected gunman in a deadly shooting in the centre of Krakow, Poland, has died in hospital, police say.
## What happened

The shooting took place in the city's Main Square on the afternoon of Saturday, 7 November 2026. Six people, four women and two men, were killed and about 16 others were injured, including visitors from the United Kingdom, Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria. Police said the 24-year-old suspect was arrested on a nearby street after trying to escape in a car, and that two officers were injured in an exchange of fire. Three more bodies were found at his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 150 kilometres from Krakow, and he is believed to have also killed three members of his own family.
## The suspect dies

In an update on Monday, 9 November, regional police confirmed that the suspect had died in hospital that morning. He is believed to have used an AR-15-style rifle, and ammunition was recovered from his car. Authorities have not given a clear motive, but said he was fascinated by far-right ideologies.
## Background
Mass shootings are rare in Poland, which has strict gun laws.
more: Six people were killed and about 16 injured.
The 24-year-old suspect died in hospital.
Police say he was fascinated by far-right ideologies.

stories.h: Kano APC council chairman freed after 68 days in kidnappers' hands
stories.p: Kano police say they have rescued Abdullahi Alasan Beli, APC chairman in Rogo LGA, after 68 days in captivity. He says his abductors moved him through parts of Kaduna and Zamfara states.
body: Kano State police say they have rescued the All Progressives Congress (APC) chairman in Rogo Local Government Area, Abdullahi Alasan Beli, popularly known as Abdullahi Fanka, after 68 days in captivity.
## The rescue

Commissioner of Police Adamu Bakori announced the rescue while briefing Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf at Government House, Kano, on Sunday, 8 November 2026, according to a statement by the state Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature Dawakin Tofa. The police chief said the rescue was achieved through coordinated tactical operations, and that the command would step up efforts against kidnapping.
## His ordeal

Beli was abducted by armed men from his home in Beli community, Rogo LGA. After his release, he said his kidnappers moved him through several places, including Danja, Ikara and Giwa in Kaduna State, as well as parts of Zamfara State.
## Reactions
Governor Yusuf, who belongs to the NNPP and is an opponent of the APC, commended the police for securing the release of the APC chieftain.
## Background
Kidnapping for ransom has affected parts of Kano, especially areas bordering Katsina and Kaduna states. It was not disclosed whether any ransom was paid.
more: Beli spent 68 days in captivity.
He says he was moved through Kaduna and Zamfara.
Governor Yusuf praised the police.

stories.h: Makinde visits families of Jos Palm Sunday attack victims
stories.p: APM presidential candidate Seyi Makinde has visited Angwan Rukuba in Jos North, Plateau State, to console families of the 33 people killed in an attack on 29 March, telling residents not to give up on Nigeria.
body: Oyo State governor Seyi Makinde, presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), has visited Angwan Rukuba in Jos North, Plateau State, to console families of victims of a deadly attack earlier this year.
## The visit

During the visit on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Makinde met residents at the home of the community head and described the killings as a national tragedy rather than a local matter. He urged the grieving community not to give up on Nigeria and assured them they were not alone. He also visited the family of Promise Gideon Ayuba, one of the victims, whose mother received him and prayed for him.
## The attack

Armed men on motorcycles attacked the Gari Ya Waye area of the community on the evening of 29 March 2026, Palm Sunday, killing 33 people. The victim's mother, Favour Ayuba, drew national attention after a video showed her placing a cutlass in her son's coffin as a demand for justice. She was also among relatives who met former Archbishop of Canterbury Justin Welby when he visited Plateau in September.
## Background

Plateau State has suffered repeated deadly attacks in recent years, with communities in Jos and surrounding areas affected. Makinde is campaigning across the country ahead of the 16 January 2027 presidential election, and his campaign this week also criticised President Bola Tinubu's claims about the naira.
more: Makinde visited Angwan Rukuba on Sunday.
Thirty-three people were killed there on 29 March.
He urged residents not to give up on Nigeria.

stories.h: Gospel singer Toluwanisings to be buried in Ibadan after family dispute
stories.p: Gospel singer Olayemi Bolaji, known as Toluwanisings, is being buried in Ibadan on Monday, almost four weeks after his death, following a dispute between his widow and his family that police helped resolve.
body: Gospel singer Olayemi Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, is being laid to rest in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Monday, 9 November 2026.
## The arrangements

According to funeral details shared on the singer's official Instagram page, the lying-in-state was scheduled for 9am to 10am, followed by a burial service from 10am to 11am at an event centre on Hope Road, Alakia, Ibadan. The announcement did not say where he would be interred.
## The dispute

Toluwanisings died in the early hours of 14 October 2026. His burial was delayed by weeks of disagreement between his widow and his family over the arrangements, reportedly including where he should be buried. The Oyo State Police Command stepped in after learning of the dispute on 28 October, with Commissioner of Police Olugbenga Abimbola helping the two sides reach an agreement.
## Background
Toluwanisings was a Nigerian gospel singer. The public dispute over his burial attracted wide attention.
more: The burial is in Ibadan on 9 November.
He died on 14 October.

stories.h: "Pharaoh, let my people go!": Cubana Chief Priest replies Umahi, accuses him of giving Tinubu fake promises on South-East votes
stories.p: Cubana Chief Priest has fired back at Works Minister David Umahi, nicknaming him "Pharaoh" and accusing him of making empty promises to President Tinubu about South-East votes. He also claimed Umahi is preparing his son to become Ebonyi governor, and mocked him with his own "money na water" catchphrase.
body: Socialite and businessman Cubana Chief Priest has replied Minister of Works David Umahi, a day after the minister mocked his famous "money na water" catchphrase and asked how many people he has given scholarships.
## "Pharaoh, let my people go"
Borrowing from the Bible story of Moses and Pharaoh, Cubana Chief Priest gave the minister a new nickname, and accused him of making promises to President Bola Tinubu that he cannot deliver.
"Pharaoh, let my people go. Stop giving Tinubu fake promises on votes. What project are you using to convince South-East people to vote for him?" he said.
## The governorship claim
He went further, claiming that Umahi is preparing his son to become governor of Ebonyi State after the current governor, Francis Nwifuru.

Speaking partly in Pidgin, he said, in effect: "You're busy preparing your son to be governor after Nwifuru. God won't let that happen. You want to use Ebonyi State to settle your child. Let the young man come and meet us on the street so we can teach him how to make 'money na water'."
This is Cubana Chief Priest's claim, and Umahi has not yet responded to this latest attack.
## How it started

The exchange began weeks ago when Cubana Chief Priest described Umahi as the second-worst minister from the South-East. Umahi hit back by telling him he was "becoming very noisy", comparing him unfavourably with Dangote and Otedola, and asking, "How many people have you given scholarships?"
Now the socialite has turned the argument back to politics, questioning what Umahi has done to win South-East votes for the President.
## Over to you
Who is winning this war of words: the minister or the socialite? And is Cubana Chief Priest right to question what the South-East has to show for supporting Tinubu?

He accused Umahi of fake promises to Tinubu on South-East votes.

stories.h: Trump admits immigration crackdown was 'too tough' after midterm defeat
stories.p: President Donald Trump has said his administration's immigration crackdown was too tough and hurt Republicans in the midterm elections, particularly the deportation of people with stable jobs whose only offence was breaking immigration rules.
body: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged that his administration's immigration crackdown went too far, in a notable change of tone after his party's heavy losses in the midterm elections.
## What he said

In an interview broadcast by the CBS programme '60 Minutes' on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Trump defended his record on border security and on removing dangerous criminals, but said he thought the crackdown had been too tough. He said the administration had suffered politically by deporting people who had stable jobs and had only committed immigration violations, and that this had hurt Republican candidates at the ballot box.
## The election

Exit polls showed immigration was the third most important issue for voters, after the economy and the state of democracy. In traditionally conservative states such as Texas, a shift among Latino voters towards the Democrats contributed to their gains in Congress, where they are projected to control both the House of Representatives and the Senate.
## Background

Mass deportations became a defining policy of Trump's second term, drawing protests and legal challenges. Only days ago he promoted Stephen Miller, the architect of the deportation programme, to White House chief of staff, so it is unclear how far policy will change in practice. Groups of Nigerians have been among those deported, including six who arrived in Lagos last week.
more: Trump says the crackdown was 'too tough'.

stories.h: Nigeria seeks $500m World Bank loan for infrastructure financing platform
stories.p: The federal government has approached the World Bank for a $500 million loan to set up a platform to attract private investment into infrastructure, part of a wider $3.85 billion programme called INFRAGROW.
body: The federal government has asked the World Bank for a $500 million loan to set up a platform to attract private investment into Nigerian infrastructure.
## The loan

According to a World Bank project document updated on 4 November 2026 and reported on Monday, 9 November, the facility is part of a broader $3.85 billion programme called the Nigeria Infrastructure Financing and De-Risking Platform for Growth and Jobs, or INFRAGROW. The Federal Ministry of Finance is listed as the borrower and the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA) as the implementing agency. The aim is to reduce the risks that discourage private investors from funding infrastructure projects.
## Why the bank says it is needed

The World Bank estimates that Nigeria has an infrastructure financing gap of about $100 billion a year, which holds back growth, competitiveness and job creation. It says the problem is not only a lack of money but also weak project preparation and difficulty turning proposals into commercially viable investments.
## Background

The request comes as President Bola Tinubu also seeks Senate approval for about $7.7 billion in new external borrowing, and as government borrowing becomes a major campaign issue. NDC candidate Peter Obi has challenged the President to account for loans, while the Presidency says claims that it has borrowed ₦120 trillion are distorted. The World Bank reported last week that Nigeria's total external debt rose to about $145 billion in 2025.
more: The $500m loan is part of a $3.85bn programme.
The NSIA would run the platform.
Borrowing is a major campaign issue.

stories.h: Makinde campaign says Tinubu cannot claim credit for naira recovery
stories.p: The campaign of APM presidential candidate Seyi Makinde has accused President Tinubu of seeking praise for the naira's recent stability after policies that sharply weakened it, saying small exchange rate gains do little for Nigerians facing high prices.
body: The presidential campaign of Oyo State governor Seyi Makinde has criticised President Bola Tinubu's claims about the naira.
## What the campaign said

In a statement reported on Monday, 9 November 2026, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, director of strategic communications for the Makinde–Daura campaign, accused the President of trying to take credit for the naira's recent stability after policies that first caused a drastic fall in its value. He said the President could not preside over the destruction of the currency's purchasing power and then ask for applause. The campaign pointed out that the official exchange rate was about ₦461 to the dollar when Tinubu took office in May 2023, before the removal of the fuel subsidy and the unification of the exchange rate, and said marginal improvements offer little relief to people facing high inflation.
## Background

The statement responds to Tinubu's remarks in Uyo last week, where he said the naira would have become worthless without his reforms and put the current rate at about ₦1,300 to the dollar. Makinde is the candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), with former DSS chief Lawal Musa Daura as his running mate, and recently launched his 'Reset Agenda' manifesto. The government has said the old official rate understated the true value of the dollar and that unification was needed.
## What happens next
The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: The campaign says the naira was ₦461/$ in May 2023.
It says small gains do not help struggling Nigerians.

stories.h: Seyi Tinubu tells Isaac Fayose to 'behave' after video criticising youths
stories.p: President Tinubu's son Seyi has hit back at businessman Isaac Fayose, who posted a video calling Nigerian youths lazy and criticising the heavy security at a City Boy Movement walk in Port Harcourt that Seyi led.
body: Seyi Tinubu, son of President Bola Tinubu, has responded to businessman Isaac Fayose after a video in which Fayose criticised young Nigerians and a pro-Tinubu walk.
## What Fayose said

In a video posted on Instagram on Saturday, 7 November 2026, Fayose used footage from a City Boy Movement walk in Port Harcourt, led by Seyi Tinubu, to question why the President's son was accompanied by a large security team of police, DSS and civil defence officers. He described Nigerian youths who turned out to support the President's re-election as lazy and distracted, pointing to insecurity in Benue, Plateau and Kogi states, deportations from the United States and hostility towards Nigerians in other African countries.
## Seyi Tinubu's response
Seyi Tinubu hit back, telling Fayose, whom he described as a content creator, to behave himself, according to reports on Monday, 9 November.
## Background

The City Boy Movement is a youth group backing Tinubu's re-election, and Seyi Tinubu has become increasingly visible in the campaign, leading walks and meeting youth groups. Isaac Fayose, a businessman and brother of former Ekiti governor Ayodele Fayose, is known for outspoken videos on social media and recently claimed that AI-generated voters could affect the 2027 elections.
more: Fayose criticised the security at Seyi Tinubu's walk.

stories.h: Hilda Baci says it is upsetting when people credit her success to her partner
stories.p: Celebrity chef and Guinness World Record holder Hilda Baci says it is sometimes upsetting when people attribute her achievements to her partner, saying it shows the mindset of many Nigerians.
body: Celebrity chef Hilda Baci has spoken out against people who credit her success to her romantic partner rather than her own efforts.
## What she said

In a video shared on Monday, 9 November 2026, the chef said such comments are sometimes upsetting and reveal the mindset of many people. Her remarks have sparked conversation about the tendency to link successful women's achievements to the men in their lives.
## Background

Hilda Baci became a household name in 2023 when she set a Guinness World Record for the longest cooking marathon by an individual, cooking for about 93 hours in Lagos. She has since built a successful food and media business. Her relationship has often been discussed on social media.
## How people reacted

Reactions were mixed. Some fans backed her, saying women deserve credit for their own work, while others joked online that her partner was better known because of her rather than the other way around.

stories.h: Portable reveals how 'Zazoo Zehh' royalties were shared with Olamide and Poco Lee
stories.p: Singer Portable says he gave Olamide 20% of the royalties from his hit 'Zazoo Zehh', up from the 16% the rapper asked for, while Poco Lee got 30%, the producer 20% and he kept 30%.
body: Singer Portable has revealed how royalties from his breakthrough hit 'Zazoo Zehh' were shared.
## What he said

In a video reported on Monday, 9 November 2026, Portable said rapper Olamide, who featured on the song, initially asked for 16 per cent because he contributed 16 bars, while the producer received 20 per cent. He said he later raised Olamide's share to 20 per cent because he felt 16 per cent was too small for an artiste of Olamide's status, and credited Olamide with helping him secure his royalties when the song came out. He said dancer Poco Lee received 30 per cent, and he kept 30 per cent for himself.
## Background

'Zazoo Zehh', released in late 2021, became a massive street anthem and turned Portable, whose real name is Habeeb Okikiola, into one of Nigeria's most talked-about artistes. The remix featured Olamide and Poco Lee. Portable has since been involved in several controversies and public disputes, but remains popular with fans of street-pop music.

stories.h: Funke Akindele and Toyosi Adesanya moment at Priscilla Ojo's store launch sparks debate
stories.p: Stars turned out for the launch of Priscilla Ojo's new store in Lagos, but a brief exchange between Funke Akindele and Toyosi Adesanya, who stood with her husband to greet her, got social media talking.
body: The opening of a new store by Priscilla Ojo, daughter of actress Iyabo Ojo, drew a crowd of celebrities in Lagos and some unexpected online debate.
## The event

Guests at the launch, reported on Monday, 9 November 2026, included Priscilla's husband, Tanzanian singer Juma Jux, as well as Mercy Aigbe, content creator Enioluwa, fashion designer Veekee James and Funke Akindele. Videos showed Iyabo Ojo greeting Funke warmly when she arrived.
## The moment that got people talking

A separate clip showed a brief interaction between Funke and fellow actress Toyosi Adesanya, who stood up with her husband to welcome her. Viewers were sharply divided over how the greeting played out, with the clip sparking wider conversation about friendships and etiquette among celebrities. Neither actress commented on the debate.
## Background

Priscilla Ojo married Juma Jux in 2025 in widely publicised ceremonies in Lagos and Tanzania. Funke Akindele is one of Nollywood's most successful filmmakers, and her new film 'The Four' recently sold out its London premiere. Iyabo Ojo also recently spoke about how she fought to get Funke roles early in her career.

stories.h: Edo consumer committee uncovers fake kpomo hub in Benin market
stories.p: The Edo State Consumer Protection Committee says it has uncovered a hub in New Benin Market where fake, chemically treated kpomo (cow skin) was being prepared and sold. Two women were arrested.
body: The Edo State Consumer Protection Committee says it has uncovered a site in Benin City where fake and chemically treated kpomo, the popular cow-skin delicacy, was being produced and sold.
## What happened

The committee's chairman, Osaro Iyamu, said officials acted on a tip-off in the early hours of Monday, 9 November 2026, and raided a spot near Efehi Street in New Benin Market. He said two women were arrested with the products, while others ran away, and that some market women later admitted to the practice. The two suspects were handed to the police for further investigation.
## The danger
Chemically treated food products can pose serious health risks, and fake kpomo has been a recurring concern in Nigerian markets.
## Background
Kpomo is widely eaten across Nigeria in soups and stews. Regulators have previously urged consumers to buy food from trusted sources.

stories.h: Naira Marley announces Marlians Fest comeback for 12 December
stories.p: Singer Naira Marley has announced the return of Marlians Fest on 12 December at Eagles Club Field in Surulere, Lagos, saying he stepped back to heal after difficult years. Davido was among those who liked the post.
body: Singer Naira Marley has announced that his Marlians Fest concert is returning this December.
## What he announced

In a long post on his social media pages on Sunday, 8 November 2026, the Marlian Records founder said the show will hold on 12 December at the Eagles Club Field in Surulere, Lagos, as part of the 'Detty December' season. He spoke about a difficult period in his life without going into detail, saying rumours and negative stories had circulated about him and that he had deliberately stepped back to find peace and heal. He described the concert as an event about growth, healing and moving forward, and dedicated it partly to everyone 'we have lost along the way'. He said friends would join him on stage and thanked supporters who stood by him.
## Background

Naira Marley became one of Nigeria's most popular street-pop stars with songs such as 'Soapy' and 'Issa Goal'. He faced intense public criticism after the death of his former signee, Mohbad, in September 2023, when questions were raised about Mohbad's earlier complaints against the label. Naira Marley was arrested and questioned by police over the death and was later released; he has denied any wrongdoing, and no charges against him have been reported in connection with Mohbad's death. A coroner's inquest was held into the circumstances. This week, VeryDarkMan has also revived discussion of the Mohbad case during his feud with Davido, while Davido's aide denied any link between the singer and Naira Marley's troubles.
## How people reacted
Davido was among those who liked the announcement on Instagram. Fans were divided, with some welcoming his return and others saying the wounds from Mohbad's death were still fresh.

stories.h: Destiny Etiko appointed Senior Special Assistant by Enugu governor
stories.p: Actress Destiny Etiko has been appointed Senior Special Assistant on Youth Engagement and Creative Economy to Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah. She is the second Nollywood star to receive a role from his administration this month, after Rachael Okonkwo.
body: Nollywood actress Destiny Etiko has been given a government appointment in Enugu State.
## The appointment

According to reports on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Etiko has been appointed Senior Special Assistant on Youth Engagement and Creative Economy to Governor Peter Mbah. The actress, who is from Udi Local Government Area of the state, confirmed the news when she responded to a congratulatory post from fellow actress Sarah Martins.
## Second Nollywood appointee

Etiko is the second prominent Nollywood figure to be appointed by the Mbah administration in a short period. Actress Rachael Okonkwo confirmed her own appointment as Senior Special Assistant on Films and Creative Industries earlier in November.
## Background

Etiko publicly supported Mbah during his campaign ahead of the 2023 governorship election. She rose to prominence after the 2014 film 'Idemili' and has since built a successful career as an actress and producer. Mbah, who was elected on the PDP platform, has since moved to the APC and backs President Bola Tinubu's re-election.
## How people reacted
Many fans and colleagues congratulated her while others had mixed reactions.
more: Etiko will advise on youth and the creative economy.

stories.h: Presidency rejects claim that Tinubu borrowed ₦120 trillion in three years
stories.p: The Presidency says viral claims that President Tinubu added ₦120 trillion to Nigeria's debt in three years are misleading, arguing that they ignore old Central Bank overdrafts added to the books in 2023 and the effect of unifying the exchange rate.
body: The Presidency has rejected viral social media claims that President Bola Tinubu's government has added ₦120 trillion to Nigeria's debt in its first three years.
## What the Presidency said

In a statement on Sunday, 8 November 2026, the President's special assistant on social media, Dada Olusegun, described the figures as a distorted picture of the country's public finances. The claim came from a widely shared graphic saying that 16 previous Nigerian leaders borrowed a total of ₦46 trillion over 63 years, compared with ₦120 trillion under Tinubu.
## The Presidency's argument

Olusegun said the ₦46 trillion figure, from late 2022, left out ₦22.7 trillion in Central Bank of Nigeria 'Ways and Means' overdrafts to the previous government, which were only formally added to the official public debt in May 2023. He also said earlier valuations of foreign debt used an official exchange rate of about ₦448 to the dollar, which understated the true naira value of those debts; when the exchange rate was unified, the naira value of existing foreign debt rose sharply even without new borrowing.
## Background

The rebuttal came after NDC candidate Peter Obi challenged Tinubu to account for subsidy savings and more than $100 billion he said the government had borrowed. The World Bank reported last week that Nigeria's total external debt, including private debt, rose to about $145 billion in 2025. Tinubu is also seeking Senate approval for about $7.7 billion in new external loans, which opposition figures have urged lawmakers to reject.
## Why it matters
Debt and the cost of living are expected to be major issues in the 16 January 2027 presidential election.

stories.h: Ghanaian singer Efya marries Nigerian singer Tómi Thomas in Accra
stories.p: Ghanaian singer Efya has married Nigerian musician Tómi Thomas in a traditional ceremony in Accra, six years after saying publicly that she would never marry. Ghana's culture minister was among the guests.
body: Ghanaian singer Efya has married Nigerian singer Tómi Thomas in a traditional ceremony in Accra.
## The wedding

The 39-year-old singer and her 33-year-old partner married on Friday, 6 November 2026, surrounded by family, friends and well-known figures from Ghana's entertainment industry, according to reports. Guests reportedly included Ghana's Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, as well as Sister Derby, Fella Makafui, Hajia4Reall, Efia Odo and Kafui Danku.
## Background

The wedding comes six years after Efya said publicly that she would never get married. The couple's relationship became public in February 2026, when their families held a knocking ceremony on Valentine's Day; their management later said that ceremony did not complete the traditional marriage rites. Efya, whose real name is Jane Awindor, is one of Ghana's best-known female vocalists. Tómi Thomas is a Nigerian singer and songwriter known for R&B and Afro-soul music.

stories.h: Hamzat vows to enforce one-year rent limit as Lagos governorship candidates debate
stories.p: Lagos APC governorship candidate Obafemi Hamzat says the state will enforce the legal limit on advance rent to one year, warning landlords against demanding two or three years upfront. He spoke at a televised governorship debate.
body: Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for governor, says the state government will enforce the legal limit on advance rent payments.
## What he said

Speaking at a governorship debate organised by a coalition of media organisations on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Hamzat said the one-year cap on advance rent is already contained in the Lagos State Real Estate Registration Agency law passed in 2025, and that the focus now is making sure it is followed. He warned landlords against demanding two or three years' rent upfront, and said estate agents are required to register with the state and appear on an official database, urging residents to check it before dealing with agents.
## The law

The Lagos State Tenancy Law of 2011 already makes it unlawful for landlords or their agents to demand more than one year's rent in advance from a new tenant, and limits advance payments from sitting tenants. Despite this, demands for two or more years' rent have remained a widespread concern.
## Rhodes-Vivour's pitch

At the same debate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, the governorship candidate of the opposition ADC, said APC governments in Lagos had focused on policies that favoured the elite for more than 20 years, while residents of poorer and rural communities did not feel the benefit of the state's high revenue. He promised more than 100,000 housing units, a safer and cleaner state, and technology-driven measures to end flooding.
## Background

Hamzat is seeking to succeed Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu in the 2027 governorship election. Former governor Akinwunmi Ambode recently pledged to mobilise support for him. Housing costs are one of the biggest concerns for Lagos residents.
more: Hamzat says the one-year rent cap will be enforced.

stories.h: House in Kano State catches fire, blaze linked to solar panel installation
stories.p: A house in Kano State has caught fire, with the blaze linked to its solar power installation. Photos show flames bursting through the roof beside the solar panels as neighbours try to help. The exact cause has not yet been confirmed.
body: A house in Kano State has caught fire, with the incident being linked to its solar power installation.
## Flames on the roof

Photos from the scene show thick smoke rising from the roof of a two-storey building, with flames breaking through beside a row of solar panels. A man can be seen climbing up to an upper-floor balcony as a crowd of neighbours gathers below, some filming on their phones and others watching in shock.
## A growing safety concern
The incident raises serious concerns about the safety of solar installations, especially as more Nigerians turn to solar energy because of unreliable electricity supply.

Poor wiring, faulty batteries, overloaded inverters and improper installation can all create fire hazards. Experts often advise homeowners to use qualified installers, buy certified equipment and have their systems checked regularly.
## Cause not yet confirmed
The exact cause of this particular fire has not yet been independently confirmed.
## Over to you
As more Nigerians embrace solar power, are we paying enough attention to proper installation and safety checks?
more: A house in Kano caught fire near its solar panels.
Faulty wiring, batteries and inverters can all cause fires.

stories.h: Another Ghanaian found dead in USA as body of 24-year-old church musician Joseph Owusu is discovered dumped near trash can in New York
stories.p: The body of Joseph Owusu, a 24-year-old Ghanaian church organist from the Bronx, was found in a large black bag left near a trash can on a Brooklyn sidewalk. CCTV footage shows two people taking the bag from a white car. Ghana's government has demanded justice.
body: The Ghanaian community in the United States has been thrown into mourning again following the disturbing discovery of the body of 24-year-old Joseph Owusu, a talented church musician who lived in the Bronx, New York.
## Found in a bag on the sidewalk
Owusu's body was discovered inside a large black bag left near a trash can on a sidewalk in Brooklyn on 30 October 2026.
CCTV footage shows two unidentified people taking the bag out of a white car, leaving it by the roadside and driving away.
## Who was Joseph Owusu?
The young man was the organist at the Ghana United Methodist Church in the Bronx. He was also studying computer science and worked as a caregiver for people living with disabilities.
## A family demands answers

His devastated family is demanding justice as investigators work to establish how he died and who abandoned his body. Ghana's embassy in the United States has confirmed his death, and the Ghanaian government has called on US authorities to ensure those responsible are found and brought to justice.
## Two young lives in days
The tragedy came just a day after another young Ghanaian, 15-year-old Javits Frimpong, was shot dead while walking to school in the Bronx.
Two young Ghanaians, two heartbreaking deaths in New York within days. Both families are now waiting for answers.
## Over to you
What is happening to these young African lives in America, and what more should be done to protect them?
more: Joseph Owusu, 24, was an organist at a Ghanaian church in the Bronx.
CCTV shows two people dumping the bag from a white car.
Ghana's government has demanded justice.

stories.h: Suspected thieves face public humiliation in South Africa as viral video sparks reactions
stories.p: A group of suspected thieves in South Africa has become the talk of social media after a video showed them lying face down in a line by the roadside, each with his face pressed against the backside of the man in front. Reactions online are split between laughter and concern.
body: A group of suspected thieves in South Africa has become the talk of social media after they were reportedly caught and subjected to an unusual form of punishment.
## The viral video

The suspects were made to lie face down on the ground in a single line by the side of a road, with each person's face pressed against the backside of the man in front of him. Their hands appear to be tied behind them.

Reports say they were caught by locals, although a uniformed officer can also be seen standing beside the men in the footage, so it is not clear whether the police or members of the public arranged them that way.
## Laughter and concern
The incident has sparked mixed reactions online. Many people found the punishment hilarious, joking that South Africans seem to have invented a brand-new style of discipline.

Others were less amused, questioning whether suspects should be humiliated in public before any court has found them guilty, and whether members of the public should ever take the law into their own hands.
## What we don't know
The circumstances of the incident, including where and when it happened and what the men are accused of stealing, have not been independently verified.
## Over to you
Is this kind of public humiliation going too far, or will it discourage stealing?
more: The suspects were made to lie face down in a line.
The video has gone viral on social media.
The circumstances have not been verified.
stories.alt: A line of suspected thieves lying face down by a roadside in South Africa with their hands tied behind them

stories.h: Amnesty International condemns Zamfara killings, says burning of 12 family members alive exposes failure of Nigerian authorities
stories.p: Amnesty International has condemned the reported killing of 12 members of one family in Zamfara State, who were said to have been burned alive, calling it another sign of the authorities' failure to protect communities from armed attacks.
body: Amnesty International has strongly condemned the reported killing of 12 members of a family in Zamfara State, describing the horrifying incident as another painful reminder of the Nigerian authorities' failure to protect innocent citizens from violent attacks.
## An entire family wiped out

Imagine an entire family wiped out in such a cruel way. Twelve human beings, reportedly burned alive. People who had their own dreams, responsibilities and hopes for tomorrow, only to have their lives cut short in circumstances no family should ever experience.

The tragedy has once again raised serious questions about the worsening security situation in parts of northern Nigeria, where many families live under the constant threat of armed attacks, kidnappings and killings.
## A failure to protect
For Amnesty International, the incident reflects a much bigger problem: the continued inability of the authorities to guarantee the safety of communities that have suffered attack after attack.

For years, residents of Zamfara and neighbouring states have endured violence from armed groups. Villages have been raided, homes destroyed, residents abducted and families forced to abandon communities where they have lived for generations.
Despite repeated assurances from government officials and security agencies, reports of fresh atrocities keep emerging.
## Every citizen deserves protection

The Nigerian government has a constitutional duty to protect lives and property. That duty extends to every citizen, whether they live in Abuja, Lagos, Zamfara or a remote village far from the attention of the national media.

The victims deserve justice, and their surviving relatives deserve more than another round of official condolences. There must be a thorough investigation, those responsible must be brought to justice, and the authorities must take meaningful steps to prevent similar tragedies.
A country cannot claim to be making progress when families are being burned alive in their homes and communities are left wondering who will be attacked next.
## Over to you
How many more innocent lives must be lost before protecting ordinary citizens becomes the government's most urgent priority?
more: 12 members of one family were reportedly burned alive in Zamfara.
Amnesty International blamed the authorities' failure to protect them.
Calls are growing for investigation and justice.

stories.h: Okowa says he left Atiku for Tinubu because he has 'seen the light'
stories.p: Former Delta governor Ifeanyi Okowa, Atiku Abubakar's running mate in 2023, told an APC rally in Port Harcourt that he switched to backing President Tinubu because he has seen the light, crediting the government's fiscal reforms.
body: Former Delta State governor Ifeanyi Okowa has explained why he abandoned former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to support President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 election.
## What he said

Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on Saturday, 7 November 2026, Okowa reportedly said he had 'seen the light'. He argued that Tinubu inherited a country with foundations weakened by decades of mismanagement, and that the current administration was making tough but necessary decisions to fix them. He credited the government's fiscal reforms with increasing the revenue shared with states and local governments, saying the results could be seen in better project delivery and salary payments. He also compared Tinubu's record as Lagos governor with his performance as President, saying the same transformation was now happening across the country.
## Background

Okowa was Atiku's vice-presidential running mate on the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) ticket in the 2023 election, which Tinubu won. He later left the PDP for the APC, following his successor in Delta, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori. Atiku is now the candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), although a Federal High Court ruling last week voided his nomination, a decision the party has appealed. At the same rally, Tinubu questioned how Atiku built a university while he was vice-president, prompting a sharp reply from Atiku's campaign.
## What happens next
Atiku's campaign had not publicly responded to Okowa's remarks at the time of writing. The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: Okowa was Atiku's running mate in 2023.
He says Tinubu's reforms have boosted state revenues.
He spoke at an APC rally in Port Harcourt.

stories.h: Six Nigerians deported from the US arrive in Lagos
stories.p: The National Emergency Management Agency says it received six Nigerians deported from the United States at Lagos airport on 4 November. The five men and one woman were profiled by immigration officers and given resettlement support.
body: Six Nigerians deported from the United States have arrived in Lagos, the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) says.
## What happened

In a statement on its X account on Sunday, 8 November 2026, NEMA said the five men and one woman, all adults, landed at the cargo terminal of Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Ikeja at about 10.13pm on Wednesday, 4 November, aboard a small chartered aircraft. NEMA's Lagos office received them in partnership with the US Consulate, the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Nigeria Immigration Service and an aviation services company. Immigration officers documented and profiled each returnee before clearing them, and NEMA said it coordinated support to help them resettle.
## Background

The deportations are part of the United States' wider crackdown on undocumented migrants under President Donald Trump, whose administration has carried out mass removals, often on chartered flights. Groups of Nigerians have been returned on several occasions over the past year. The agency did not give the reasons for the individual deportations. Trump this week named Stephen Miller, the architect of his deportation programme, as White House chief of staff.
## What happens next
NEMA said the federal government would continue to work with other agencies to manage the return of Nigerians from abroad in an orderly and dignified way.
more: Five men and one woman were deported.
They arrived in Lagos on 4 November.
NEMA says it is helping them resettle.

stories.h: All 10 passengers abducted from commercial bus in Ogun regain freedom, one suspected kidnapper killed
stories.p: All 10 passengers kidnapped from a commercial bus at Orita Fufu, Awa-Ijebu, Ogun State, on 3 November have been released unharmed, police say. One suspected kidnapper was killed in a follow-up operation, and an AK-47, ammunition and ₦1.37 million were recovered.
body: There is good news from Ogun State: all 10 passengers abducted from a commercial bus at Orita Fufu, Awa-Ijebu, have regained their freedom.
## Released unharmed
The passengers were taken on Tuesday, 3 November 2026. Police say they were released unharmed on the night of Saturday, 7 November, following sustained security pressure and intelligence-led efforts.
## Suspect killed, weapons and cash recovered
During a follow-up operation, police say one suspected kidnapper was killed. An AK-47 rifle, ammunition, ₦1.37 million in cash and a mobile phone were reportedly recovered.
Photos of the recovered items show bundles of naira notes, an AK-47 magazine and a mobile phone laid out on the ground in the bush.
## Questions still unanswered
Police have not said whether any ransom was paid for the passengers' release.
Reports also differ on whether any of the passengers was a serving or recently discharged member of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC).
## Safe at last
The most important update is that all 10 passengers are alive and safely out of captivity, after five days that must have been terrifying for them and their families.
The incident is another reminder of the danger travellers face on Nigeria's highways, and of the need for security agencies to keep up pressure on kidnapping gangs.
## Over to you
What more should be done to make Nigeria's highways safe for travellers?
more: All 10 passengers were freed unharmed.
One suspected kidnapper was killed; an AK-47 and ₦1.37m were recovered.
Police have not said whether a ransom was paid.

stories.h: Flamingos get $50,000 reward, but no FIFA prize money for World Cup win
stories.p: Nigeria's U-17 world champions, the Flamingos, have received a $50,000 cash gift from a sponsor of the National Sports Commission at a reception in Rabat. FIFA does not pay prize money for the tournament because it is classed as a developmental competition.
body: Nigeria's Flamingos have received a $50,000 cash reward after winning the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, but the team will not receive any official prize money from FIFA.
## The reward

The gift was presented by Alhaji Saleh Ahmadu, a sponsor of the National Sports Commission (NSC), at a reception held in the team's honour in Rabat, Morocco, on Saturday night, 7 November 2026, according to reports. The event was hosted by NSC chairman Shehu Dikko and director-general Bukola Olopade, and was also attended by the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi. The sponsor said the gift recognised the players' outstanding performance, commitment and determination.
## No FIFA prize money

FIFA classifies the U-17 Women's World Cup as a developmental tournament and does not attach official prize money to it, unlike the senior World Cups. That means the champions receive the trophy and medals but no payment from world football's governing body.
## How the final was won

The Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 in the final on Saturday. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring when her looping effort slipped through the hands of Japan's goalkeeper, and Oluebube Umejiaku doubled the lead with a lob after a through ball from Esther Stephen. Japan's Fuki Ito pulled one back with ten minutes left, but Nigeria held on to become the first African winners of the tournament.
more: A sponsor gave the team $50,000 in Rabat.
FIFA pays no prize money for the U-17 Women's World Cup.
Nigeria beat Japan 2-1 in the final.

stories.h: Tinubu to inaugurate sections of Kaduna–Kano and Kano–Maradi railways on 3 December
stories.p: President Tinubu will inaugurate completed sections of the Kaduna–Kano and Kano–Katsina–Maradi railway projects on 3 December, according to his campaign council. It says the Kaduna–Kano line is about 90% complete.
body: President Bola Tinubu has fixed 3 December 2026 for the inauguration of completed sections of two major railway projects in northern Nigeria.
## The projects

According to a statement on Sunday, 8 November 2026, by Dele Alake, spokesman of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, the 203-kilometre Kaduna–Kano Standard Gauge Railway is about 90 per cent complete, while the 400-kilometre Kano–Katsina–Maradi line, which will link Nigeria with the Republic of Niger, is about 70 per cent complete. The 190-kilometre Jaji-to-Kano segment of the Kaduna–Kano line and the 250-kilometre Dawanu–Kano–Kazaure–Daura–Katsina stretch of the Kano–Maradi line are due to be inaugurated on 3 December.
## Progress claims

The statement said that when Tinubu took office in 2023, the Kano–Maradi project was barely 5 per cent complete and the Kaduna–Kano line under 30 per cent. It said a federal inspection team led by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Funso Adebiyi, recently assessed both corridors and carried out a test run. The figures come from the President's campaign and have not been independently verified.
## Background

The Kaduna–Kano line is part of the planned Lagos–Kano standard gauge railway, which already runs from Lagos to Ibadan and from Abuja to Kaduna. The Kano–Maradi project was started under former President Muhammadu Buhari.
## Why it matters
The inauguration will come just weeks before the 16 January 2027 presidential election, and infrastructure is a key part of the President's re-election campaign.
more: Sections of both lines open on 3 December.
The Kaduna–Kano line is said to be 90% complete.
The figures come from Tinubu's campaign.

stories.h: Lagos seals Surulere church over noise pollution after resident's complaint
stories.p: The Lagos State environment ministry has sealed All Christians Gathering Ministry in Surulere on Sunday morning after a resident complained online about noise. Commissioner Tokunbo Wahab said it will stay closed until further notice.
body: The Lagos State Government has sealed a church in Surulere over noise pollution.
## What happened

The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, said on his X account on Sunday, 8 November 2026, that All Christians Gathering Ministry, located off Clegg Street in Surulere, had been shut and would remain closed until further notice. He said the action followed a complaint from a resident on X about noise from the church, and that officials investigated and confirmed the complaint was valid, finding the church in breach of environmental regulations. The sealing took place on Sunday morning.
## No exceptions
Wahab said the government would not soften its position on such violations, whether the offender is a religious body, a business or anyone else.
## Background

The Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency has sealed many churches, mosques, hotels, clubs and event centres in recent years over noise pollution, often after complaints on social media. Wahab is known for responding publicly to residents' complaints online. Just this week, another Lagos resident cried out to the commissioner over noise from a church at midnight.
more: The church was sealed on Sunday morning.
A resident had complained on X.
Commissioner Wahab says there will be no exceptions.

stories.h: VeryDarkMan challenges Zlatan Ibile to deny sending celebrities to beg him
stories.p: VeryDarkMan has dared Zlatan Ibile to publicly deny that he secretly sent celebrities to plead with him over their ongoing feud, accusing the singer of acting tough in public while trying to settle the matter behind the scenes. He has threatened to name the celebrities.
body: Social media activist VeryDarkMan (VDM) has continued his public exchange with singer Zlatan Ibile, daring him to openly deny claims that he secretly sent celebrities to plead with VDM over their ongoing disagreement.
## "Just come out and say it's a lie"

Speaking partly in Pidgin, VDM said, in effect: "It's been over 24 hours since I dared Zlatan to come out and say I'm lying that he sent people to beg me. He acts like a hard guy in public, but does something else behind the scenes."
"Just come out and say it's a lie, simple! Let me call out the names of the celebrities you sent. If they deny it too, then you'll see what my next post will be."

He added that he was only holding back out of respect for Zlatan's parents: "It's because your mother and father are involved. We still respect parents here. If not, everyone would already know that you have no class."
## Tough in public, soft in private?
VDM claims Zlatan is acting tough in public while making moves behind the scenes to settle the matter, and has threatened to name the celebrities he says were sent if Zlatan stays silent.

The feud began after a video of Davido singing a line from Zlatan's song INFERNO at Zlatan's wedding welcome party in Morocco, a lyric VDM believes was aimed at him. VDM then warned Zlatan that he would "learn the hard way".
## Allegations, not facts
For now, these remain VeryDarkMan's claims. Zlatan has not responded publicly, and his silence does not confirm them.
## Over to you
Will Zlatan respond, or will he let VDM keep controlling the conversation?
more: VDM says Zlatan secretly sent celebrities to beg him.
He has threatened to name them.
Zlatan has not responded publicly.

stories.h: "You're becoming very noisy, 'money na water'!": Umahi fires back at Cubana Chief Priest, questions his wealth and contributions to society
stories.p: Works Minister David Umahi has hit back at Cubana Chief Priest, weeks after the celebrity businessman called him the second-worst minister from the South-East. Umahi mocked his famous "money na water" catchphrase and asked how many people he has given scholarships.
body: "You're becoming very noisy. Money na water. How much do you have? Have you ever seen Dangote saying, 'I have money,' or Otedola saying that he's rich? Money speaks for itself. It's not by saying money na water. What have you done? How many people have you given scholarships?"

Those were the strong words of Nigeria's Minister of Works, David Umahi, as he fired back at Cubana Chief Priest, weeks after the celebrity businessman described him as the second-worst minister from the South-East.
## "Money speaks for itself"

The criticism clearly did not go down well with the former Ebonyi State governor, who has now turned the conversation towards wealth, public conduct and what rich people are doing to improve the lives of others.
Umahi questioned the constant public display of wealth, particularly the expression "money na water" (meaning money flows like water), which Cubana Chief Priest is widely known for.

He pointed to two of Nigeria's richest businessmen, Aliko Dangote and Femi Otedola, and asked whether Nigerians regularly hear them announcing how much money they have. For Umahi, genuine wealth should speak through achievements, investments and contributions to society, not constant declarations on social media.
## The scholarship question
The line that stands out most is his question: "How many people have you given scholarships?"
That question takes the argument beyond who has more money. It raises a different issue entirely: what impact are wealthy Nigerians making in the lives of ordinary people?
## Two different conversations

Cubana Chief Priest has every right to criticise a public officeholder, and Umahi, as a serving minister, is equally entitled to respond. But criticism of a minister's performance is ultimately best answered with evidence of work done, projects completed and results delivered.

That is what makes this exchange interesting. Umahi is questioning Cubana Chief Priest's display of wealth, while the original criticism was about Umahi's performance as Minister of Works. These are two different conversations, and Nigerians will have their opinions on both.
## Over to you

Does Cubana Chief Priest need to prove how many people he has helped before he can criticise a serving minister? Or should Umahi focus on defending his performance in office rather than questioning another man's wealth?
more: Cubana Chief Priest called Umahi the second-worst South-East minister.
Umahi mocked his 'money na water' catchphrase.
He asked how many people CP has given scholarships.

stories.h: Bandits reportedly kill 12 members of one family in Zamfara village attack
stories.p: Twelve members of the same family were reportedly killed when bandits set fire to the building where they had taken refuge during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun LGA, Zamfara State. Other residents were said to have been kidnapped.
body: Twelve members of one family have reportedly been killed in an attack by bandits on a village in Zamfara State.
## What happened

The attack took place late on Saturday, 7 November 2026, in Gidan Taba village, Dosara Birnin Kaya ward, in Maradun Local Government Area, according to residents. A resident said the head of the family had gathered his relatives into a single room to try to stop them from being kidnapped. When the attackers found the family and they refused to come out, the bandits reportedly set the building on fire, and all 12 people inside died. An unknown number of other residents were reportedly abducted during the raid. The victims were buried according to Islamic rites on Sunday morning.
## Official response
The police and the Zamfara State Government had not publicly commented on the attack at the time of writing.
## Background

Zamfara is one of the states worst affected by banditry in Nigeria's North-West, with armed groups carrying out killings, mass kidnappings and attacks on farming communities. Last week, bandits ambushed a bus carrying police officers on the Sokoto–Gusau road, reportedly killing and abducting some of them. Security forces have carried out repeated operations in the state's forests, but attacks on villages continue.
more: Twelve family members were reportedly killed.
Other residents were reportedly abducted.
The attack happened in Maradun LGA.

stories.h: Amaechi warns court ruling against ADC could trigger unrest if mishandled
stories.p: ADC vice-presidential candidate Rotimi Amaechi has warned that the court judgment removing the party's leadership and voiding Atiku Abubakar's nomination could lead to serious unrest, even civil war, if the dispute is not properly managed.
body: Rotimi Amaechi, the vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has warned that the court ruling against the party's leadership could cause serious unrest if it is not handled carefully.
## What he said

In comments reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Amaechi said the judgment that nullified the party's leadership and the process that produced Atiku Abubakar as presidential candidate could lead to civil war if the dispute is not properly managed. He did not set out in detail how he believed the crisis should be resolved.
## The ruling

On Thursday, Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja ruled that the national working committee led by former Senate President David Mark was invalid. The judgment also nullified the emergence of former Interior Minister Rauf Aregbesola as national secretary, and decisions taken by the Mark-led leadership, including the process that produced Atiku as candidate. The court directed INEC not to recognise decisions taken at the party's national executive committee meeting of 27 July 2025. The suit was filed by Nafiu Gombe, a former deputy national chairman of the party.
## Background

The ADC has appealed the judgment and asked INEC not to act on it until the appeal is heard. Atiku has vowed to stay in the race and accused the government of using the courts against the opposition. Amaechi, a former Rivers governor and transport minister, this week also said former President Muhammadu Buhari had promised in writing to back him in 2022.
## What happens next
Attention is now on the Court of Appeal and on how INEC responds before the presidential election on 16 January 2027.
more: Amaechi says the ruling could cause unrest if mishandled.
The court voided Atiku's nomination last week.
The ADC has appealed.

stories.h: Gift Orban overtakes injured Osimhen in Turkish league scoring race
stories.p: Super Eagles striker Gift Orban scored his 10th Turkish Süper Lig goal of the season for Amedspor, moving one ahead of the injured Victor Osimhen in the race for the Golden Boot, though Amedspor lost 4-3 to Galatasaray.
body: Nigerian striker Gift Orban has moved ahead of Victor Osimhen in the race to be top scorer in Turkey's Süper Lig.
## The goal

Orban scored his 10th league goal of the season for Amedspor in their 4-3 defeat away to Galatasaray, reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026. After a quiet first half, the former Lyon striker headed home from close range from a cross by substitute Furkan Soyalp. Another Nigerian, Yira Sor, also scored for Amedspor after coming off the bench, but Galatasaray held on to win.
## The scoring race

The goal took Orban to 10 goals and five assists in 11 league appearances, one more goal than Osimhen, who has nine goals and three assists in eight league games. Osimhen missed the match after having knee surgery on Saturday to remove a loose body from his left knee, and is expected to be out for at least three weeks.
## Background

Orban joined Amedspor on loan in the summer transfer window. He made his name at Belgian club Gent, where he scored freely, before moving to Lyon. Osimhen, the 2023 African Player of the Year, has been out of action since the Champions League win over Stuttgart. Both are Super Eagles strikers, and with Osimhen ruled out of the AFCON qualifiers against Tanzania this month, Orban's form will interest Nigeria's coaching staff.
more: Orban has 10 league goals this season.
Osimhen has nine but is injured.
Amedspor lost 4-3 to Galatasaray.

stories.h: Iran says two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz
stories.p: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines while using unauthorised routes through the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels were not named. The incident comes days after US strikes on Iranian targets.
body: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says two oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
## What Iran said

In a statement carried by Iran's state news agency on Sunday, 8 November 2026, the Guards said one tanker struck a mine in the eastern part of the strait and the other elsewhere in the waterway, while trying to cross using routes not authorised by Tehran. The statement did not name the vessels or give their nationalities, and accused them of violations including switching off their navigation and tracking systems. There was no independent confirmation of the incidents or of any casualties.
## Background

Iran has sharply restricted shipping through the strait since a war began in late February, requiring ships to follow routes it has approved. The United States responded with a naval blockade of Iranian ports and has helped tankers pass through the waterway, which normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil. Iran has reported several ships catching fire in the strait in recent weeks. The incident comes days after US forces struck an Iranian air defence site on Qeshm Island, an operation President Donald Trump described as minor.
## Why it matters
Disruption in the Strait of Hormuz affects global oil supply and prices, which in turn affect Nigeria's oil revenue and the cost of imported fuel.
more: Two tankers reportedly hit mines in the strait.
Iran says they used unauthorised routes.
The vessels have not been named.

stories.h: Saidi Balogun hits back at critics over his campaigning for Tinubu
stories.p: Nollywood actor Saidi Balogun has responded to online attacks over videos of him hosting campaign rallies for President Tinubu, urging people to respect others' political choices.
body: Nollywood actor Saidi Balogun has responded to criticism over his open support for President Bola Tinubu's re-election bid.
## What happened

The actor had shared videos on social media showing him hosting campaign rallies for the President in different parts of the country, which drew strong criticism from some social media users. In a response reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Balogun refused to back down, urging critics to allow people to hold different political views without being attacked.
## Background

Balogun is a veteran actor, producer and director in the Yoruba film industry. He is one of several entertainers who have appeared at Tinubu's campaign events in recent weeks, alongside others such as actress Eniola Badmus, who also posted a video this week explaining why she believes the President deserves a second term.
## The wider debate

The involvement of entertainers in the 2027 campaigns has divided opinion online. Some argue that public figures have every right to back the candidates they choose, while others say supporting the government amounts to endorsing economic hardship. The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: Balogun has hosted rallies for Tinubu.
He urged critics to respect political differences.
Other celebrities have also joined campaigns.

stories.h: Tony Elumelu celebrates daughter's Oxford master's degree
stories.p: Billionaire businessman Tony Elumelu has celebrated his eldest daughter, Ogechukwu, on earning a Master of Science degree from the University of Oxford while also completing a law conversion course.
body: Billionaire businessman and philanthropist Tony Elumelu has celebrated his eldest daughter, Ogechukwu, after she earned a master's degree from the University of Oxford.
## What happened

In a social media post on Saturday, 7 November 2026, Elumelu shared a video from the graduation ceremony, saying his daughter had achieved two major milestones: a Master of Science degree from Oxford and the completion of a law conversion course. The video showed the family celebrating together.
## Background

Ogechukwu, also known as Tamara-Marie Oge Elumelu, is the daughter of Tony Elumelu and his wife, Dr Awele Elumelu. She previously graduated with honours from the London School of Economics, where she studied politics and philosophy. Tony Elumelu is the chairman of Heirs Holdings and the United Bank for Africa (UBA), and founder of the Tony Elumelu Foundation, which supports young African entrepreneurs. He made headlines recently with a gift at singer Zlatan Ibile's wedding.
## How people reacted
The post drew congratulatory messages from followers and public figures.
more: Ogechukwu Elumelu earned an MSc from Oxford.
She also completed a law conversion course.
She previously studied at the LSE.

stories.h: Nkem Owoh denies saying Yoruba founded Nollywood, credits them with pioneering films
stories.p: Veteran actor Nkem Owoh, known as Osuofia, has said on a popular interview show that he never claimed the Yoruba founded Nollywood, pointing out that the word did not exist when he started acting, but credited Yoruba filmmakers such as Hubert Ogunde with pioneering the tradition.
body: Veteran Nollywood actor Nkem Owoh, popularly known as Osuofia, has addressed comments attributed to him about who founded Nigeria's film industry.
## What he said

Speaking on the YouTube interview show 'Curiosity Made Me Ask', hosted by content creator Isbae U, in an episode uploaded on Saturday, 7 November 2026, Owoh rejected reports that he had said the Yoruba people started Nollywood rather than the Igbo. He explained that the word 'Nollywood' did not even exist when he and his colleagues first began making films. However, he said Yoruba filmmakers had indeed pioneered the home-video tradition in Nigeria, giving particular credit to the late theatre and film pioneer Hubert Ogunde. When the host jokingly suggested Ogunde might have been Igbo, Owoh insisted that he was Yoruba.
## The wider debate

The question of who built Nollywood has been debated for years. In August 2026, the late actor Francis Duru argued that Igbo businesspeople were the real architects of the home-video boom of the 1990s and early 2000s, while accepting that the Yoruba film community had become more dominant through stronger organisation. Owoh was reported at the time to have pointed out that Yoruba filmmakers were active in theatre and film long before the video boom. Duru died in October 2026.
## Background

Owoh is one of Nollywood's best-loved comic actors, famous for the 'Osuofia in London' films and the song 'I Go Chop Your Dollar'. 'Curiosity Made Me Ask' is one of Nigeria's most popular celebrity interview shows.
more: Owoh says he never claimed the Yoruba founded Nollywood.
He credited Hubert Ogunde as a pioneer.
He spoke on 'Curiosity Made Me Ask'.

stories.h: CBN sets ₦15bn capital rule for dollar-backed stablecoins in new crypto rules
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria has set minimum capital of ₦10 billion for naira-backed stablecoin issuers and ₦15 billion for those offering dollar or other foreign-currency tokens, under new rules for crypto operators. Other crypto service providers will need ₦1 billion.
body: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has introduced tougher rules for cryptocurrency and stablecoin businesses, including minimum capital requirements of up to ₦15 billion.
## The new requirements

Under the regulations, reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026, issuers of naira-backed stablecoins must have at least ₦10 billion in paid-up capital, while operators offering tokens backed by foreign currencies, such as dollar-pegged stablecoins, will need ₦15 billion. Other virtual asset service providers, including digital wallet, payment, transfer and custody businesses, must have at least ₦1 billion. The CBN said it may demand more capital from larger or riskier operators.
## Licensing and foreign firms

The rules make it illegal for individuals or companies to issue, exchange, distribute or facilitate regulated virtual assets in Nigeria without CBN approval. Foreign operators targeting Nigerian customers must incorporate and obtain licences locally, regardless of approvals elsewhere. Companies already licensed by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) will face extra capital requirements if they offer services under the CBN's oversight, while digital assets classed as securities will remain under SEC supervision. The rules also set standards for reserve management and consumer protection.
## Deadlines and fines

The regulations, released on Friday, give existing operators 30 days to register with the CBN, 60 days to begin submitting supervisory reports and 180 days to complete licence applications. Operators can continue at their current scale during the transition, but those who miss the deadline must suspend operations until licensed. Firms operating without approval face fines starting at ₦100 million.
## Background

Nigeria has one of the world's largest communities of cryptocurrency users. The CBN banned banks from dealing with crypto firms in 2021 before lifting the restriction in 2023, and the SEC has since moved to register and regulate crypto exchanges. Stablecoins, which are designed to keep a steady value linked to a currency such as the dollar, are widely used by Nigerians for savings and payments.
more: Dollar-backed stablecoin issuers need ₦15 billion in capital.
Naira-backed issuers need ₦10 billion.

stories.h: MultiChoice shuts down GOtv Stream app months after closing Showmax
stories.p: MultiChoice has discontinued its GOtv Stream mobile app, telling users to go back to their decoders, without giving a reason. It is the latest change since French group Canal+ took over the company, following the closure of Showmax in April.
body: MultiChoice has shut down its GOtv Stream app, which allowed subscribers to watch selected GOtv channels on phones and tablets.
## What happened

A notice on the GOtv Stream website, reported on Sunday, 8 November 2026, confirmed the closure and directed customers back to their television decoders. The app has also been removed from the Google Play Store and Apple App Store; app-tracking data showed the Android version was removed on 21 October. Before the closure, it offered live channels, catch-up programmes and offline downloads, depending on the subscription package. MultiChoice has not given a reason for the shutdown or announced a replacement.
## Background

GOtv Stream launched in Nigeria on 1 December 2023 as part of MultiChoice's effort to let subscribers watch TV away from their living rooms. The closure is the latest change since French media group Canal+ took control of MultiChoice in a deal valued at about $2 billion, which became unconditional in September 2025. MultiChoice announced in March 2026 that it would close its Showmax streaming service, citing heavy losses, and Showmax shut down in April, with subscribers directed to DStv Stream. The company has also recently dropped the Africa Magic Family channel after 12 years.
more: The GOtv Stream app has been discontinued.

Showmax closed in April.

stories.h: Opeyemi Falegan apologises to Nkechi Blessing on TikTok Live years after split
stories.p: Ekiti politician Opeyemi Falegan has publicly apologised to actress Nkechi Blessing Sunday during a TikTok Live session, years after their messy 2022 break-up. Nkechi said his past remarks about her were still being used against her.
body: Ekiti politician Opeyemi Falegan has publicly apologised to Nollywood actress Nkechi Blessing Sunday, years after their much-discussed break-up.
## What happened

The apology came during a TikTok Live session on Saturday, 7 November 2026, in which the former couple spoke face to face online about their 2022 separation. Nkechi made it clear that she wanted a genuine apology, reminding Falegan that remarks he made about her during a social media live session years ago were still circulating and being used against her. She also said that despite their fallout, she had defended him in comment sections when people criticised him.
## Falegan's response

Falegan apologised and said he had grown since their split, urging both of them to let the past go. He also spoke about what he described as emotional unavailability and temperament issues on both sides that made the relationship difficult.
## Background

Nkechi Blessing is a popular actress and producer known for her outspoken personality on social media. Her relationship with Falegan was widely publicised before it ended in 2022 amid public exchanges online. The actress was also recently in the news after confronting comedian Carter Efe and his girlfriend.
## How people reacted
Fans were divided, with some praising the two for making peace and others questioning why Nkechi chose to revisit the matter in public.
more: Falegan apologised during a TikTok Live.
The couple split in 2022.
Fans were divided over the public reunion.

stories.h: Obi asks Tinubu to account for subsidy savings and over $100bn in loans
stories.p: NDC candidate Peter Obi has challenged President Tinubu to explain what his government has done with the ₦15.8 trillion reportedly saved from fuel subsidy removal and more than $100 billion in borrowing, a day after Tinubu criticised Obi's record in Anambra.
body: Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has called on President Bola Tinubu to account for money saved from the removal of the fuel subsidy and from government borrowing.
## What Obi said

In a statement on his X account on Saturday, 7 November 2026, titled 'Good Day, Mr President: Nigerians Deserve Accountability', Obi said the large sums flowing into government coffers, including higher tax revenues, should be producing clear improvements in Nigerians' daily lives. He urged the President to visit the remaining 33 states he has not yet toured, spend time with the people and explain what his administration had done with the ₦15.8 trillion he said had been saved from subsidy removal, the more than $100 billion he said had been borrowed, and increased revenue from taxes.
## The background to the exchange

Obi's statement came a day after Tinubu, speaking in Akwa Ibom, criticised the former Anambra governor's record on erosion in the state. At a reception in Uyo the same day, Tinubu said the naira would have become worthless without his reforms and that Nigeria would never go back to the subsidy. Vice-President Kashim Shettima also told an APC rally in Uyo that Obi had run himself out of the race.
## The figures

Obi did not give a breakdown of how he arrived at the figures. The World Bank reported this week that Nigeria's total external debt, including private-sector debt, rose to about $145 billion in 2025. The government says its borrowing is needed to fund infrastructure and that its reforms have saved the economy from collapse.
## What happens next
The Presidency had not publicly responded to Obi's statement at the time of writing. The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: Obi cited ₦15.8 trillion in subsidy savings.
He said Tinubu had borrowed over $100 billion.

stories.h: Van Vicker says viral photos of him with Regina Daniels are AI-generated
stories.p: Ghanaian actor Van Vicker has dismissed viral photos appearing to show him with Nollywood actress Regina Daniels, saying they were created with artificial intelligence and that the two have not been in contact for more than a decade.
body: Ghanaian actor Van Vicker has dismissed viral images appearing to show him with Nollywood actress Regina Daniels, saying they were generated using artificial intelligence.
## The photos

According to reports on Sunday, 8 November 2026, one of the images showed Van Vicker carrying a much younger Regina Daniels, while another placed him beside her during what looked like her recent birthday photoshoot. The pictures spread widely online and caused a stir among fans of both actors.
## What he said
Van Vicker said neither image was real, and that he and Regina Daniels had not been in contact for well over a decade. He spoke out quickly to stop the rumours from spreading further.
## Background

Van Vicker is one of the best-known Ghanaian actors in Nollywood and has starred in many Nigerian films since the mid-2000s. Regina Daniels, who began acting as a child, has been in the news recently, including a public clash with journalist Kemi Olunloyo, and new videos from the mansion of her husband, Senator Ned Nwoko, have also drawn attention online. The case is the latest example of AI-generated images of celebrities spreading on social media and being mistaken for real photos.
more: Van Vicker says the photos were made with AI.
